about: The FLR Hub Assistant's approved help. Everything here is public (this site is), so it holds how-to text only: no names, email addresses, records, codes or private links. Links are relative to the Hub; a tool whose address lives in the FLR database is linked by its tile id and only shown to people whose Hub has that tile. 'ask' is how people might ask, 'keys' are extra words it can be found by, 'who' is who can do it (admin, estimator, approver or driver). 'care' marks a topic that's a worry or about privacy, which the assistant answers with a reassuring face rather than a celebration. 'alsoPeople' lists words the help uses in its own names that are also people's first names ("the Jeff Day", "Likkle Jeff"): in a question they're taken for a person unless they're part of one of those names. 'data' names the look-up in records.js that answers with the person's own records (read-only) when they're signed in and have the tool. Check changes with: node assistant/tests/run.mjs

entries.title: What Likkle Jeff can do
ask: what can the assistant help with
can the assistant do things for me
entries.answer:
I’m Likkle Jeff, the Hub’s assistant. I find answers in its help and link you to the right page. I can also look up your own records, read-only: your leave, who’s off, your driving and the Estimator’s quotations. I show only what your tools would show you, and I can’t change anything: booking, approving and editing happen in the tools.

If the help doesn’t cover something, I’ll say so rather than guess.

entries.title: What’s on the Hub
ask: what tools are on the hub
what can I do on the hub
what is the flr hub for
what can I use the hub for
entries.answer: The FLR Hub is the home for FLR’s staff tools: the Cost Estimator, Fleet Management, Annual Leave and the Fitter Schedule. It shows the tools your account can use. Hover over an icon, or press and hold it on a phone, to see what it does.

entries.title: Sign in
ask: how do I log in to the hub
entries.answer:
Sign in on the Hub with your FLR email address and password. One sign-in opens the Hub’s tools on that device, including the Cost Estimator; the Fitter Schedule also asks for a team passcode.

If your password isn’t accepted, use “Forgotten your password?” below the “Sign in” button.

entries.title: Create an FLR account
ask: how do I create an account
I'm new, how do I get access
make an account for the hub
entries.answer: On the Hub’s sign-in screen, choose “Create an account”. You’ll need your full name, your work email, a password of at least 10 characters with letters and numbers, and the access code from an FLR Super Admin. A Super Admin then checks who you are and switches on your tools.
steps: Open the Hub and choose “Create an account”, below “Sign in”.
Enter your full name and work email, then a password and the same password again under “Confirm”.
Enter the access code from an FLR Super Admin.
Press “Create account”.
Wait for a Super Admin to check who you are. Your tools appear on the Hub once they’re on.

entries.title: Waiting for your tools
ask: I've registered but I can't see any tools
my hub says waiting for a super admin
I made an account and nothing is there
how long until my tools are switched on
entries.answer: New accounts wait until a Super Admin checks it’s really you, using your usual work number or Teams, or through IT. They then switch on your tools, which appear on the Hub. You don’t need to do anything. If it’s been more than a working day, ask a Super Admin.

entries.title: Get the access code
ask: where do I get the access code
my code isn't accepted when I sign up
entries.answer:
You only need the access code to create an account. Ask an FLR Super Admin for it: it isn’t written anywhere on the Hub, and I don’t know it.

If it isn’t accepted, check it with a Super Admin, as it may have changed.

entries.title: Reset a forgotten password
ask: I'm locked out of my account
entries.answer: On the Hub’s sign-in screen, choose “Forgotten your password?”, enter your email and press “Send reset link”. The link in the email opens “Choose a new password”; enter it twice and press “Save password”.

entries.title: Change your password
ask: how do I change my password
entries.answer: In the Cost Estimator, press your name at the top right (your initials on a phone), then “Change password…”. You can also set a new one from the Hub’s sign-in screen with “Forgotten your password?”.

entries.title: Sign out
ask: sign out on a shared computer
entries.answer: On the Hub, press the round button with your initials at the top, then “Sign out”. It signs you out of the Hub and its tools on this device.

entries.title: A tool is missing from your Hub
ask: a tool is missing from my hub
I can't see a tool on the hub
how do I get access to a tool
some of my tools didn't load
why can't I see the same tools as my manager
it says I don't have access to the cost estimator
annual leave says I don't have access
why can't I open fleet management
entries.answer:
Your Hub shows the apps your account can use: FLR Super Admins choose them in Hub settings. If one you need isn’t there, or an app says you don’t have access, ask an FLR Super Admin.

If the Hub says “Some of your tools didn’t load”, press “Try again”.

entries.title: Your account is switched off
ask: it says my FLR account is switched off
entries.answer: If a page says your FLR account is switched off, only an FLR Super Admin can switch it back on, in Hub settings. Ask one to check it.

entries.title: Manage accounts and app access
ask: how do I give someone access to an app
turn off someone's access to an app
switch the cost estimator on for someone
where do I manage accounts now
send someone else a password reset
which apps does a new account get
change which apps a person can use
entries.answer: FLR Super Admins look after every account in Hub settings: the gear beside your initials on the Hub. New accounts wait under “New accounts waiting” until you’ve checked who they are. Each person has a switch for each app; their name opens their role, a switch for the whole account and a password reset. Registration, the access code and what new accounts get are under “Registration”.

entries.title: Check and switch on a new account
ask: how do I approve a new account
someone has registered, what do I do
check who someone is before switching them on
switch on someone who has just registered
how do I check a new account is genuine
entries.answer: In Hub settings, new accounts are listed under “New accounts waiting”. Open the person, check it’s really them with contact details FLR already holds (their work number from the staff list, Teams on their existing work account, or IT) and write a short note. Then choose their role and tools, tick the box and confirm. If you can’t confirm who it is, turn the account down: it stays switched off.
steps: Open Hub settings and find the person under “New accounts waiting”.
Contact them using details FLR already holds, never ones that came with the sign-up.
Say how you checked, add a note (when, and the IT ticket number if IT checked), choose the role and tools, and tick the box.
Confirm. Their tools appear on their Hub straight away.

entries.title: Admins and Super Admins
ask: what's the difference between an admin and a super admin
what can a super admin do
why can't an admin open hub settings
entries.answer: Super Admins look after accounts, roles, app access, registration and every app’s settings. Admins do the day-to-day work: they approve leave and see everyone’s, see every driver and fitter arrivals, and reassign quotations, but can’t see or change any settings. Your role is shown in your account on the Hub.

entries.title: Get back to the Hub
ask: how do I get back to the hub
go back to the home page
what does the flr logo do
is the logo a link to the hub
entries.answer: Press the FLR logo at the top of any tool, or use your browser’s Back button. The link below goes there too.

entries.title: Change the name on your account
ask: how do I change my name
change the name on my quotes
entries.answer: In the Cost Estimator, press your name at the top right (your initials on a phone), change “Your name (as shown on quotations and in the change log)” and press “Save”.

entries.title: Switch between light and dark
ask: how do I turn on dark mode
entries.answer: The Hub and the Cost Estimator follow your device’s light or dark setting. To choose one for the Cost Estimator, press your name at the top right (your initials on a phone), then “Appearance”. Fleet Management has its own light and dark button at the top, and the Fitter Schedule has “Switch theme”.

entries.title: About the Cost Estimator
entries.answer: The Cost Estimator builds FLR’s flooring quotations in four stages: “Project details”, “Rooms”, “Review costs” and “Client quotation”. It opens from the Hub already signed in.

entries.title: Start a new estimate
ask: how do I start a new estimate
start a quote for a new job
how do I price up a new job
entries.answer: In the Cost Estimator, press “Create new quotation” on the Projects page, then use the next FLR number or type an existing FLR reference.
steps: Open the Cost Estimator. It opens on Projects.
Press “Create new quotation”. If it asks you to complete your profile, add your name and press “Save and continue”.
Press “Create with the next FLR number”, or type a reference such as Q-2026-041 under “Or use an existing FLR reference” and press “Create with this reference”.
Fill in “Project details”, then press “Continue to rooms”.

entries.title: Add rooms to an estimate
ask: how do I add a room
add another room to a quote
entries.answer: On the “Rooms” stage, press “Add first room”, fill in the room or area name, project type, who measured it and the specified floorcovering, then press “Save room” or “Save and add another”. Saved rooms have “Edit”, “Duplicate”, “Copy ×…” and “Delete”.

entries.title: Find a quotation
ask: where can I find an old quote
look up a quote by client
entries.answer: On the Cost Estimator’s Projects page, search by quote ID, client or site, or pick a group: “All”, “Recently edited”, “Drafts”, “Ready to quote”, “Approved” or “Archived”. Choose yourself under “All estimators” to see only yours, then press “Open” or the quote ID.

entries.title: Approve a quotation
ask: how do I approve a quote
the quotation is ready, what next
entries.answer: Once the rooms are saved, mark the costs as reviewed, check the client quotation and approve it. Approving prints it.
steps: On “Review costs”, press “Mark costs as reviewed”, then “Review client quotation”.
Check the quotation. “Full-screen preview” helps.
Tick “I have reviewed this quotation and its wording”.
Press “Approve and print quotation”.

entries.title: Print or save a quotation as PDF
ask: how do I print a quote
save a quotation as a pdf
get a pdf of an estimate
entries.answer: A quotation prints when you approve it with “Approve and print quotation”. After that, open it and press “Print again”. For a PDF, choose “Save as PDF” as the printer.

entries.title: Change an approved quotation
ask: how do I change an approved quote
edit a quote after it's approved
update a quote that's already been sent
add a room to a quote that's already approved
entries.answer: An approved quotation stays as it was approved. Open it and press “Create revision” to make a new version you can change.

entries.title: Copy a quotation
ask: how do I copy a quote
use an old quote as a template
make a copy of a quote
entries.answer: On the Projects page, open the quotation’s “More” menu and choose “Duplicate”.

entries.title: Archive or delete a quotation
ask: how do I delete a quote
get rid of a test quote
entries.answer: On the Projects page, open the quotation’s “More” menu and choose “Archive”. Archived quotations are under “Archived”, where “Restore” brings them back. Only FLR Super Admins can delete a quotation.

entries.title: The four stages of a quotation
ask: what are the stages of a quote
why can't I open the client quotation
it says save a room first
it says resolve the blocking issues first
entries.answer: Every quotation goes through “Project details”, “Rooms”, “Review costs” and “Client quotation”. A stage stays locked until the one before is done: it tells you why, for example “Save a room first” or “Resolve the blocking issues first”.

entries.title: What your role allows in the Cost Estimator
ask: why can't I create a quote
what does the developer role do
it says my role can view quotations but not create them
what's the difference between admin and estimator
what does the user role mean
entries.answer: Users can create, edit, approve and archive quotations. Admins can also reassign them; Super Admins can also delete them and change the Cost Estimator’s settings. Developers can view and export quotations but not create or change them. Your role is shown in your account on the Hub; Super Admins change it in Hub settings.

entries.title: Change prices, rules or quotation wording
ask: how do I change the prices
add a product to the catalogue
entries.answer: FLR Super Admins set prices, rules and wording in the Cost Estimator’s Settings: “Catalogue”, “Commercial rules”, “Price overrides” and “Quotation settings”.
steps: Open the Cost Estimator and choose “Settings” in the bar at the top (at the bottom on a phone).
Pick “Catalogue”, “Commercial rules”, “Price overrides” or “Quotation settings”.

entries.title: Give a quotation to another estimator
ask: how do I reassign a quote
change the estimator on a quote
hand a quote over to someone else
entries.answer: FLR Admins and Super Admins can move a quotation to another estimator with “Reassign…” on the quotation.

entries.title: What the cost terms mean
ask: what does materials mean in the costs
entries.answer: On the “Review costs” stage, open “What the terms mean” for an explanation of each figure.

entries.title: About Fleet Management
entries.answer: Fleet Management shows speeding by driver and vehicle from FleetView, covering the last 30 days and updated every 15 minutes through the working day. FLR Admins and Super Admins see every driver and vehicle. A driver whose FLR account is linked to their FleetView name sees only their own driving; anyone else sees nothing until a Super Admin links them.

entries.title: Find the driver speeding report
ask: where can I find the driver speeding report
entries.answer: The driver speeding report is Fleet Management on the Hub. Admins and Super Admins see every driver; a driver linked to their FLR account sees their own driving.

entries.title: See your own driving
ask: how do I see my driving
entries.answer: Open Fleet Management. If your FLR account is linked to your FleetView name, it opens on “My driving”, with your incidents and FleetView performance, then “Map” for where they happened and “My vehicle” for your vehicle’s dates. Only you and FLR Admins and Super Admins can see your page.

entries.title: Fleet Management shows nothing
ask: fleet management says nothing to show you yet
why can't I see anything in fleet management
my account isn't linked to a driver
entries.answer: “Nothing to show you yet” means your FLR account isn’t linked to your FleetView driver name. Ask an FLR Super Admin to link it; then you’ll see your own driving.

entries.title: Link a driver to an FLR account
ask: how do I link a driver to an account
connect a driver to their sign in
give a driver access to their report
entries.answer: FLR Super Admins link each FleetView driver to their FLR account in Fleet Management. A linked driver sees only their own page.
steps: Open Fleet Management on the “Drivers” page.
Under “Driver sign-ins”, press “Manage sign-ins”.
Find the driver, choose their FLR account and press “Link” (or “Unlink”).
Use “Preview” to see exactly what they’ll see.

entries.title: Review drivers
entries.answer: The “Drivers” page lists drivers in review order, most urgent first. Narrow it with the status chips (“Needs review”, “Priority”, “Above average”, “At or below”, “Limited evidence”), the search, vehicle type, period and sort.

entries.title: How the speeding report works
entries.answer:
An incident is a recorded speed at or above the limit plus 10% plus 2 mph, such as 35 in a 30. It isn’t an allowance. Serious incidents are 20 mph or more over. Drivers are grouped by incidents per 100 miles against the fleet rate, and under 150 miles is “Limited evidence”.

“How this report works” on the Drivers page explains it all.

entries.title: See the worst speeding incidents
entries.answer: Fleet Management lists each serious incident: 20 mph or more over the limit. Admins and Super Admins see the whole fleet’s on the map and each driver’s page; a linked driver sees their own. Speed limits come from FleetView’s mapping and can be wrong, so check the location.

entries.title: Look at a speeding incident
ask: how do I see where an incident happened
see an incident on google maps
entries.answer: Open an incident to see when and where it happened, with “Open in Google Maps”. Admins and Super Admins also get “Open in FleetView” and the driver and vehicle details. Speed limits come from FleetView’s mapping and can be wrong, so check the location.

entries.title: Use the speeding map
entries.answer: Open “Map” in Fleet Management. Choose “Incidents” or “All events”, narrow it with “Filters”, and press “Fit all” to see everything. The “Incident list” shows the same incidents as a list.

entries.title: Check MOT, tax and service dates
ask: when is the road tax due
when is the mot due on registration
who drives the van with registration
which vans need an mot this month
entries.answer: Admins and Super Admins: the “Vehicles” page starts with “Needs action” (a passed date Monday also calls Overdue) and “Needs checking” (a passed date Monday doesn’t call Overdue, or a missing date), then what’s due in the next 30 days. Search by plate, driver or model; each vehicle has “Open in Monday”. Linked drivers: see “My vehicle”.

entries.title: When the fleet data updates
ask: how often is the speeding report updated
it says data is out of date
entries.answer: Speeding figures come from FleetView via the FLR Fleet Management updater, a Chrome add-on on an FLR Super Admin’s computer. It sends them every 15 minutes while that computer is on, so not overnight, at weekends or on FLR close days. Monday board vehicle details update every 15 minutes. If the figures stop updating in the working day, Admins and Super Admins see a notice; tell an FLR Super Admin if it stays.

entries.title: Who can see your driving
ask: can other drivers see my speeding
can my manager see my speeding
entries.answer: Only you and FLR Admins and Super Admins can see your page. Drivers never see other drivers or the review order.

entries.title: An incident that wasn’t you
ask: someone else was driving my van
the report shows a journey I didn't do
entries.answer: FleetView records events against a vehicle, so the name shown is the vehicle’s assigned driver, who may not have been driving at the time. If an incident wasn’t you, tell an FLR Admin or Super Admin which one.

entries.title: About Annual Leave
ask: what is the annual leave page
entries.answer: Annual Leave shows who’s off today, your days left, your leave requests and any other leave such as sick or unpaid leave, with the “Request leave” button. Leave approvers also get “Approvals”, “Diary” and “All requests”, and selecting a name in the Diary opens that person’s leave record.

entries.title: Request annual leave
ask: where do I request annual leave
how do I book a holiday
entries.answer:
In Annual Leave, choose “My Leave” and press “Request leave”: the leave form opens in a new tab. Your request then shows under “Your requests” once it reaches monday.com, and a leave approver decides.

If there’s no “Request leave” button, ask a leave approver for the form.
steps: Open Annual Leave and choose “My Leave”.
Press “Request leave” and fill in the leave form.
Check “Your requests” for the decision. “Refresh” updates it.

entries.title: See how many days you have left
ask: how many days holiday do I have left
how much annual leave have I got
who can see my leave balance
how many days does someone have left
entries.answer: In Annual Leave, choose “My Leave”. The big number under “Days left in …” is your balance for that leave year, with “Bookable”, “Accepted”, “Waiting for a decision” and “Left if accepted”. Use “Leave year” to switch years. Only you and leave approvers can see it.

entries.title: Check on a leave request
ask: the status of my holiday request
has my leave request been approved
entries.answer: In Annual Leave, choose “My Leave” and look under “Your requests”: each request shows its decision. A new request can take a few minutes to appear; press “Refresh” to check again.

entries.title: Annual Leave says you aren’t linked
ask: my account isn't linked to a staff record
annual leave says I'm not linked
entries.answer: Your leave appears once your work email is on your record in the “FLR - Leave Allowances” board. Ask a leave approver to add it.

entries.title: Cancel or change booked leave
ask: how do I cancel my holiday
I don't need the day off any more
entries.answer:
Ask a leave approver. They can cancel accepted leave, which puts the days back into your allowance, or re-open a request.

Approvers: open the request, then “Cancel leave” or “Re-open”.

entries.title: See what’s waiting for approval
ask: leave still waiting to be decided
entries.answer: Leave approvers see every request waiting for a decision on the “Approvals” tab, each with Annual Leave’s own suggestion: accept, review or deny. Everyone else sees their own requests on My Leave.

entries.title: Approve or decline leave
ask: how do I approve a holiday request
approve time off for my team
entries.answer: Leave approvers use “Approvals” in Annual Leave. Each request has a suggestion; press “Accept”, “Review” or “Deny”, with an optional note. Accepting against the suggestion asks you to confirm. If you don’t see “Approvals”, you aren’t a leave approver.
steps: Open Annual Leave and choose “Approvals”.
Open “Details” to check the request and the suggestion.
Add a note if you like, then press “Accept”, “Review” or “Deny”.

entries.title: See who’s off
ask: who is on holiday on a date
entries.answer: “Today” in Annual Leave shows who’s off today, for everyone. Staff see names, groups and whether it’s all day or half, not the kind of leave. Leave approvers also see the kind of leave and when people are back, and can look further ahead in the “Diary”.

entries.title: See everyone’s days left
ask: how much leave has the team got left
who has the most leave left
who has the least holiday left
entries.answer: Leave approvers can see anyone’s allowance and days left in Annual Leave: open the “Diary” and select their name. Their leave record also lists their requests and other leave, such as sick or unpaid leave.

entries.title: What the diary colours mean
ask: what do the colours mean in the diary
what do the colours in the calendar mean
entries.answer: In the “Diary”, press “Colour key” to see what each colour means, including bank holidays, company close days and the Jeff Day.

entries.title: Bank holidays and company close days
ask: do bank holidays come out of my allowance
is the christmas shutdown taken from my holiday
does the jeff day count as holiday
when are the bank holidays this year
what are the christmas shutdown dates
what are the company close days
entries.answer: Bank holidays and the Jeff Day are on top of your allowance. Company close days (when FLR closes over Christmas) are set aside from it, and My Leave shows how many. My Leave also lists the year’s bank holidays and company close days under “Request leave”; switch the year to see next year’s.

entries.title: Share the leave form
ask: how do I share the leave form
where is the leave form link
entries.answer: Leave approvers can press “Copy form link” at the top of Annual Leave and send it on. Everyone else opens the form with “Request leave”.

entries.title: About the Fitter Schedule
ask: what does the fitter schedule show
how far ahead does it go
entries.answer: The Fitter Schedule shows which fitters are working, free or off on each day from 30 days ago to 30 days ahead, and which jobs still need a fitter. It opens from its tile on the Hub and asks for the team passcode.

entries.title: Find a free fitter
entries.answer: In the Fitter Schedule’s “Day” tab, pick a date in the day strip (30 days back to 30 ahead; “Today” comes back), then choose “Free”. Each day is split into “Needs a fitter”, “Working”, “Free” and “Unavailable”, and “Search fitter or job” finds someone quickly.

entries.title: The Fitter Schedule passcode
ask: what's the passcode for the fitter schedule
do I need to log in for the fitter schedule
entries.answer: The Fitter Schedule opens with the team passcode, not your Hub sign-in. Ask the office for it: it isn’t on the Hub, and I don’t know it. If you’re also signed in to the Hub on that device, it shows fitters’ photos and number plates. “Change passcode” is at the foot of the schedule.

entries.title: What Working, Free, Off and Clash mean
ask: what does off mean on the fitter schedule
what do the colours mean on the fitter schedule
why is a fitter showing as off
entries.answer: A fitter is “Working” on a day if a job overlaps it, “Off” (under “Unavailable”) if they’re on leave, off sick, at an appointment or not working, and “Free” otherwise. “Clash” means work and leave on the same day. Jobs with no fitter are under “Needs a fitter”.

entries.title: See one fitter’s days
ask: what is a fitter doing this week
what did a fitter do last week
entries.answer: Open the “Fitter” tab in the Fitter Schedule and use “Choose a fitter” to see their days from today to 30 days ahead. Their last 30 days are under “Earlier”.

entries.title: Find jobs that need a fitter
ask: see all the fitters on a job
which fitters are booked on a job
entries.answer: In the Fitter Schedule’s “Jobs” tab each job shows once with all its fitters. Choose “Needs fitter” for jobs still missing one, or search by job, postcode or fitter. Tap a job to see each person’s dates, whether they’re Scheduled or TBC and, for Admins and Super Admins, today’s arrival, with “Open in monday.com”.

entries.title: Show weekends, subcontractors or completed jobs
ask: show weekends on the fitter schedule
entries.answer: Open “Settings” in the Fitter Schedule: “Show weekends”, “Use the weekend rota”, “Show FLR staff and subcontractors” and “Include jobs already marked Completed”.
